steps.message:
# Ship is damaged when performing the action shown in the recording

### What happens
`recording.mp4` shows a ship performing an action at a station. The action does not
go the way it is set up to go, and the ship does not come out of it unharmed.
The ship takes damage from the very start of the action shown in the video, before it visibly hits anything. Both the ship's and the station's models are involved. Nothing else about the ships or stations should change.

### Expected
Performing the action shown in the recording must not damage the ship at all, at the spot shown in
the video or at any other equivalent spot of the same station. The hull-integrity readout stays at
100% for the whole action.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

You can inspect the video frame by frame with `ffmpeg` (installed in the image), e.g. extracting
still frames at specific timestamps to look closely at the HUD and the ship.

Inspect the attached file before making changes. The video describes observable behavior; it does
not prescribe source files, internal names, or an implementation strategy.

I made a fix and it compiles, but I couldn't confirm it against the recording or in the running game. `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4` is missing (the folder is empty and there's no copy anywhere on the system), so I worked out the cause from the code alone. Please check that it matches what the video shows.

**What I think the recording shows:** manual takeoff from a landing pad on a spinning orbital station. This code path (`Player::DoFixspeedTakeoff`, `src/Player.cpp:347-359`) is meant to avoid the pad: the code comment says it lifts the ship clear "with a margin". It only did so in a token way:
- it moved the ship up just **0.01 m** from where it sits on the pad;
- it gave it just **0.05 m/s** of outward speed.

The ship takes on the station's spin when it launches. Because of that spin, points on the ship away from its centre get up to about 0.06 m/s × their distance moving toward the pad's surface. The collision code doesn't account for the station's own motion. So for almost any ship, 0.05 m/s outward is too little, and parts of the hull register as moving into the pad. With a 1 cm gap the meshes touch straight away, and the collision counts as a crash with nothing visibly hitting. Every pad on a spinning station is affected the same way, which matches "any equivalent spot of the same station". Planet pads and planet takeoffs don't spin, so they weren't affected.

**Fix (`src/Player.cpp`), two values changed:**
- The starting lift is now **0.5 m** instead of 0.01 m.
- The outward speed is now **2 m/s** instead of 0.05 m/s. That is the same as the 2 m/s cruise speed the takeoff already asks for, so the autopilot doesn't have to fight it.

At the fastest station spin (0.062 rad/s), 2 m/s keeps every point within about 32 m of the ship's centre moving away from the pad. That covers ships that fit the largest pads. Nothing else about ships, stations, docking or damage rules was changed.

**Checked:** the project builds cleanly with `ninja`.

**Not checked:** I didn't launch the game or fly a takeoff to confirm the hull stays at 100%. My earlier ideas were damage checks during pad landings and pad positions stored in the model files; the code didn't support the first, and the model files have no history to compare against. If the video actually shows something other than manual takeoff from an orbital pad, tell me what it shows and I'll look again.
